# PermissionDiff 0.1.0

PermissionDiff's first public release makes authorization changes reviewable in CI. Declare the
subjects, resources, actions, contexts, and invariants that matter to your application; capture a
trusted baseline; then replay the exact same corpus against candidate code.

## Highlights

- Detect newly allowed and newly denied authorization paths with deterministic baseline replay.
- Check tenant isolation, role boundaries, ownership, and custom invariants.
- Generate meaningful cases and shrink counterexamples with Hypothesis.
- Preserve stable case fingerprints and create minimized JSON reproductions for failures.
- Use `init`, `test`, `snapshot`, `diff`, and `explain` from the CLI.
- Use readable terminal output, complete machine-readable reports, and stable exit codes in CI.
- Run the CLI directly or use the thin `abishekgiri/permissiondiff@v0` composite action.

## Install

```bash
pip install permissiondiff==0.1.0
```

Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 are supported.

## Important security note

PermissionDiff evaluates trusted Python authorization code in a timeout-controlled subprocess,
which provides fault isolation, not a hostile-code security sandbox. Run it in an isolated
development or CI environment and do not connect
test authorizers to production systems, secrets, or side effects.

This alpha release supports local Python authorizers only. Remote policy-engine adapters,
AI-agent runtime interception, and dashboards are not implemented. Reproducible findings require
deterministic authorizers and matching package, Python, configuration, seed, and corpus inputs.

See the [README](https://github.com/abishekgiri/permissiondiff#readme) for the quickstart and
[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/abishekgiri/permissiondiff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete
feature and limitation list.
